key_insight: Macrocanonical generator networks learn fast physics surrogates by matching multiscale statistics in expectation, allowing realistic variation across generated samples.
engineering_relevance: Once trained, these generators replace costly per-sample simulation or optimization with a single forward pass for uncertainty quantification and simulation-based inference workflows.
method: Train a neural generator to match target multiscale statistics in expectation rather than for each sample.
Amortize symmetry-preserving sample-space optimization into one generator training run.
Use near-identity residual generators and small learning rates to locally preserve entropy early in training and mitigate mode collapse.
evidence_signal: Cosmology and fluid experiments report realistic samples from very small training sets, sometimes one example, with per-sample generation over 10^6 times faster than reference simulators and over 10^3 times faster than microcanonical gradient descent.
watch_item: Matching selected statistics does not by itself establish accuracy for every downstream observable; validate task-specific behavior before replacing a simulator.
paper_title: Macrocanonical Generator Networks: Data-Efficient Neural Surrogates for Amortized Physics Simulation
